site.name: PARIS / LE BOURGET
site.desc: First confirmed hantavirus case in France: one of five repatriated Hondius passengers tested PCR-positive; critically ill French woman now on artificial lung (ECMO) at Bichat Hospital Paris per AP 12 May. French government mandated 42-day quarantine decree with contact tracing identifying 22 potential cases across international flights.

site.name: GEORGIA
site.desc: Two American Hondius passengers transferred to Emory University Hospital SCDU (Serious Communicable Diseases Unit) in Atlanta for monitoring as of 12 May per Emory/Axios; two additional Georgia residents from same cruise asymptomatic and following CDC guidance at home. Emory stated no public risk anticipated. Emory SCDU, established 2002, is one of few US facilities capable of treating dangerous communicable diseases.

site.name: NEBRASKA
site.desc: Nebraska Medicine / UNMC National Quarantine Unit (NQU) received two Americans in biocontainment units: one asymptomatic PCR-positive per AP News 11 May, one symptomatic per The Daily Beast — travel content creator Jake Rosmarin among those quarantined, reporting feeling safe under medical care. 17 Americans total repatriated via State Dept airlift from Tenerife to Offutt AFB; CDC says widespread US transmission unlikely.

site.name: PRAIA
site.desc: Hondius anchored Praia 03–06 May; refused docking by Cape Verde per The Week. Three medevac patients evacuated 06 May — two flew Amsterdam (hazmat teams at Schiphol), third plane made unscheduled Gran Canaria refueling stop after Morocco refused permission + medical equipment malfunction. Dr. Stephen Kornfeld (oncologist aboard) coordinated with global health experts during this period per The Atlantic.
